q: What is the capital of Burkina Faso?
x: The name is often shortened by locals to 'Ouaga', and the city is known for its film festival, FESPACO.

q: What is the capital of Kyrgyzstan?
x: The city lies on the northern edge of the Tian Shan range and has a regular grid of tree-lined streets.

q: What is the capital of Azerbaijan?
x: Baku sits on the Caspian Sea and is among the lowest-lying capitals in the world.

q: What is the capital of Georgia, the country in the Caucasus?
x: Tbilisi is known for its sulfur baths and sits on the Kura River.

q: What is the capital of Armenia?
x: The city is one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities and has views of Mount Ararat.

q: What is the capital of North Macedonia?
x: Mother Teresa was born in Skopje in 1910.

q: What is the capital of Albania?
x: Its center, Skanderbeg Square, is named for the country's national hero.

q: What is the capital of Slovenia?
x: A dragon appears on the city's coat of arms, and the compact capital is known for its riverside cafes.

q: What is the capital of Malawi?
x: Lilongwe became the capital in 1975, replacing Zomba.

q: What is the capital of Madagascar?
x: Locals often shorten the name to Tana, and the city is built on hills in the island's central highlands.

q: What is the capital of Namibia?
x: Its name roughly translates as 'windy corner' in Afrikaans.

q: What is the capital of Suriname?
x: Its historic inner city is a UNESCO World Heritage site, with wooden buildings from the Dutch colonial period.

q: What is the capital of Paraguay?
x: Founded in 1537, it is one of the oldest cities in South America.

q: What is the capital of Bhutan?
x: It is one of the few world capitals without traffic lights.

q: What is the capital of Papua New Guinea?
x: The city has no road link to the rest of the country's major towns.

q: What is the capital of Oman?
x: The city lies between rugged mountains and the Gulf of Oman.

q: What is the capital of Cyprus?
x: It is one of the last capitals in Europe still divided by a buffer zone.

q: What is the capital of Nicaragua?
x: The city sits on the shore of Lake Managua, in a region prone to earthquakes.

q: What is the capital of Lithuania?
x: Its Baroque Old Town is one of the largest surviving medieval old towns in Europe.

q: What is the capital of Slovakia?
x: It is the only national capital that borders two other countries, Austria and Hungary.

q: What is the capital of Haiti?
x: Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.

q: What is the capital of the US state of Alaska?
x: Juneau cannot be reached by road from the rest of the state, only by air or sea.

q: What is the capital of the Canadian province of British Columbia?
x: The capital sits on Vancouver Island, not on the mainland.

q: Which ocean trench contains Challenger Deep, the deepest known point in Earth's oceans?
x: At roughly 10,900 meters deep, it is deeper than Mount Everest is tall.

q: Which is the world's largest landlocked country by area?
x: It stretches more than 3,000 km from the Caspian Sea to the Altai Mountains.

q: What is the highest mountain on the Australian mainland?
x: At 2,228 meters it is the lowest of the highest peaks of the seven continents.

q: What is the highest mountain in Antarctica?
x: It rises about 4,892 meters in the Ellsworth Mountains and was first climbed in 1966.

q: The vast white Salar de Uyuni salt flat is in which country?
x: After rain, it becomes a giant mirror and holds a huge share of the world's lithium reserves.

q: Which large salt lake in the middle of Australia is often dry?
x: It lies about 15 meters below sea level and fills only when floods come, perhaps a few times a century.

q: Which desert along Namibia's Atlantic coast gave the country its name?
x: It is thought to be the oldest desert in the world and has some of the tallest sand dunes.

q: The Taklamakan Desert lies in the western part of which country?
x: It is surrounded on three sides by mountains and once lay along parts of the Silk Road.

q: The Thar Desert spans the border of India and which other country?
x: It is one of the most densely populated deserts in the world.

q: Which huge sand desert covers much of the southern Arabian Peninsula and is nicknamed the Empty Quarter?
x: Covering around 650,000 square kilometers, it is one of the largest continuous sand deserts in the world.

q: The Karakum Desert covers most of which Central Asian country?
x: The name means 'black sand', and the Darvaza gas crater, known as the 'Door to Hell', burns within it.

q: The Strait of Malacca separates the Malay Peninsula from which large island?
x: It is one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world, linking the Indian and Pacific Oceans.

q: Which strait separates mainland Australia from Tasmania?
x: It is named after surgeon George Bass, who explored it in 1798.

q: Which strait separates New Zealand's North and South Islands?
x: The strait is only about 22 km wide at its narrowest but is notorious for rough weather.

q: Which stretch of sea between Cape Horn and Antarctica is known for some of the roughest waters on Earth?
x: About 800 km wide, it is where the Atlantic, Pacific and Southern Oceans mix.

q: The Strait of Hormuz links the Persian Gulf to which gulf?
x: A large share of the world's seaborne oil passes through the strait, which is only about 39 km wide at its narrowest.

q: The Dardanelles strait connects the Aegean Sea to which sea?
x: The ancient Greeks called it the Hellespont, and the legend of Hero and Leander is set along it.

q: Bab-el-Mandeb, whose name means 'Gate of Tears', links the Red Sea to which body of water?
x: It lies between Yemen on the Arabian Peninsula and Djibouti and Eritrea in Africa.

q: Which strait separates India from Sri Lanka?
x: The shallow strait is dotted with a chain of limestone shoals known as Adam's Bridge.

q: The Sargasso Sea is unusual among seas because it has what feature?
x: It is bounded entirely by ocean currents inside the North Atlantic and is named for floating Sargassum seaweed.

q: How many countries have a coastline on the Caspian Sea?
x: They are Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan, and it is the world's largest inland body of water.

q: Which landlocked microstate on Mount Titano is entirely surrounded by Italy?
x: It claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic, founded in 301 AD.

q: How far ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is India Standard Time?
x: India uses a single time zone with a half-hour offset and does not observe daylight saving time.

q: Which large country officially uses just one time zone, despite spanning about five geographic ones?
x: The whole country runs on Beijing time, so the sun rises very late in the far west.

q: Which Himalayan country uses a time zone that is 5 hours 45 minutes ahead of UTC?
x: It is one of the few places in the world with a 45-minute offset.

q: Roughly which line of longitude does the International Date Line follow?
x: It zigzags around some countries and island groups so that they stay on the same calendar day.

q: Which mountain is the second-highest in the world?
x: Located on the China-Pakistan border in the Karakoram range, it is considered harder and more dangerous to climb than Everest.

q: What is the highest mountain in the British Isles?
x: It is in the Scottish Highlands, reaches 1,345 meters, and its summit is clouded for most of the year.

q: What is the highest mountain in New Zealand?
x: Its Maori name means 'cloud piercer', and it rises 3,724 meters in the Southern Alps.

q: Mount Olympus, the mythical home of the Greek gods, is the highest mountain in which country?
x: Its highest peak, Mytikas, rises to about 2,917 meters.

q: Mount Ararat, the traditional resting place of Noah's Ark, is the highest peak in which country?
x: The dormant volcano rises to roughly 5,137 meters near the borders with Armenia and Iran.

q: Mount Erebus, the southernmost active volcano on Earth, is on which continent?
x: It sits on Ross Island and contains a long-lived lava lake.

q: In which country is the active volcano Popocatépetl?
x: Its name means 'smoking mountain' in the Aztec language, and it lies within sight of a megacity.

q: The 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens happened in which US state?
x: The blast removed about 400 meters from the summit and is the deadliest volcanic event in US history.

q: The rock-hewn churches of Lalibela are in which country?
x: Eleven medieval churches were carved down into solid volcanic rock in the 12th and 13th centuries.

q: The relocated rock temples of Abu Simbel were saved in the 1960s from flooding by which lake?
x: Engineers cut the temples into huge blocks and rebuilt them on higher ground.

q: The Maya city of Chichen Itza is on which Mexican peninsula?
x: Its main pyramid, El Castillo, casts a snake-shaped shadow on the equinoxes.

q: The giant Buddhist temple of Borobudur is on which Indonesian island?
x: Built in the 9th century, it is the world's largest Buddhist temple.

q: The Potala Palace, once the winter residence of the Dalai Lama, overlooks which city?
x: It stands at more than 3,600 meters above sea level and has over 1,000 rooms.

q: The ancient rock fortress of Sigiriya is in which country?
x: The 5th-century citadel sits atop a granite column about 180 meters high.

q: The monasteries of Meteora perch on towering rock pillars in which country?
x: The name means 'suspended in the air', and monks once hauled supplies up in nets.

q: The granite spires of Torres del Paine National Park are in which country?
x: The park is in Patagonia and is a classic trekking destination, famed for its 'W' circuit.

q: The Cliffs of Moher, rising over the Atlantic, are on the west coast of which country?
x: They rise to about 214 meters and stretch for around 8 km.

q: Yellowstone National Park and its Old Faithful geyser lie mostly in which US state?
x: Established in 1872, it is generally regarded as the first national park in the world.

q: Lake Louise, famed for its turquoise water, is in which Canadian province?
x: The color comes from fine rock flour carried into the lake by meltwater from glaciers.

q: The fairy-chimney landscapes of Cappadocia are in which country?
x: People carved homes, churches and entire underground cities into the soft volcanic rock.

q: Whitewashed Santorini belongs to which Greek island group?
x: The island is the rim of a volcanic caldera formed by a huge eruption about 3,600 years ago.

q: Which isthmus joins Africa to Asia?
x: The Suez Canal now cuts through it, technically making the Sinai Peninsula a part of Asia separated from Africa by water.

q: What is a dry riverbed in the deserts of North Africa and Arabia called?
x: It can suddenly flood with rushing water after a distant rainstorm.

q: What is the name for ground that stays frozen for at least two years in a row?
x: Large areas of Siberia, Alaska and Canada sit on it.

q: What is a long, deep sea inlet carved by a glacier called?
x: The word is Norwegian, and Norway, Chile, New Zealand and Greenland all have famous examples.

q: What is a ring-shaped coral island that encloses a lagoon called?
x: Darwin proposed that atolls form as a volcanic island sinks and its fringing reef keeps growing upward.

q: Which semi-arid belt of Africa lies just south of the Sahara?
x: The name comes from the Arabic word for 'shore', since it forms the edge of the great desert.

q: Which African lake is the second deepest in the world?
x: It is also the world's longest freshwater lake, stretching about 670 km in the Great Rift Valley.

q: Which river is the longest in Australia?
x: It flows about 2,500 km from the Australian Alps to the sea near Adelaide.

q: Which river flows past Montreal and Quebec City into the Gulf of the same name in eastern Canada?
x: With the Great Lakes, it forms a shipping route that leads deep inland into North America.

q: Which river rises in Guinea, loops through Mali, and ends in a vast delta on the Gulf of Guinea?
x: It takes a boomerang-shaped path, flowing away from the nearby ocean before looping back toward it.

q: Which river forms much of the border between Russia and China in the Far East?
x: It flows about 2,800 km before reaching the Sea of Okhotsk.

q: Which river flows from Lake Geneva through the French city of Lyon?
x: It flows into the Mediterranean through a delta called the Camargue.

q: Which river flows through both Warsaw and Kraków in Poland?
x: It is the longest river in Poland and empties into the Baltic Sea near Gdańsk.

q: Which is the longest river entirely within France?
x: It is known for its valley of castles, including Chambord and Chenonceau.

q: The Arctic archipelago of Svalbard is a territory of which country?
x: It is home to a global seed vault buried in permafrost.

q: The spice island of Zanzibar is part of which country?
x: Zanzibar joined with mainland Tanganyika in 1964 to form the modern country.

q: Which island nation in the Indian Ocean is the lowest-lying country on Earth?
x: Its highest natural point is only a couple of meters above sea level.

q: Which Pacific island country is the world's smallest republic?
x: It covers only about 21 square kilometers and has no official capital city.

q: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
x: Much of this coastline is on islands in the Arctic Archipelago.

q: What is the capital of the Canadian territory of Nunavut?
x: It was formerly called Frobisher Bay, and the territory was created in 1999.

q: What is the highest mountain in the contiguous United States?
x: It rises 4,421 meters in California's Sierra Nevada, less than 140 miles from the lowest point in North America.

q: Which Central Asian country is doubly landlocked, meaning all its neighbors are landlocked too?
x: One would have to cross at least two borders to reach an ocean from there.

q: Which South American country takes its name from the Spanish word for the equator?
x: The country was named for the equatorial line that passes just north of its capital.

q: Which country has more ancient pyramids than Egypt?
x: The Kushite rulers built over 200 steep-sided pyramids, many around Meroë.

q: Which bay in eastern Canada is famous for having the highest tides in the world?
x: Tidal range can exceed 15 meters, and each tide moves more water than all the world's rivers combined.

q: Which line of latitude, at about 66.5 degrees north, marks the southern limit of the midnight sun?
x: North of this line the sun stays above the horizon for at least one full day each summer.

q: Which landlocked East African country did Winston Churchill call the 'Pearl of Africa'?
x: Churchill praised its lush landscapes and wildlife in a 1908 book.

q: Which cape, rather than the Cape of Good Hope, is the southernmost point of Africa?
x: The Cape of Good Hope is roughly 150 km to the northwest and is often wrongly given the title.

q: Mount Elbrus, often named as Europe's highest peak, belongs to which mountain range?
x: It is a dormant volcano in southern Russia, about 5,642 meters high.

q: Lake Constance borders Germany, Switzerland and which other country?
x: The Rhine flows into the lake and out again, and there is no agreed border line on the water.
